metadata-description: Learn how Ethereum can support organizations that need open, verifiable ways to coordinate, while understanding the trade-offs.
hero-description: Ethereum is open infrastructure for people and organizations that need to coordinate without giving one operator permanent control over the system.
paths-description: Whether you are evaluating a product, a public service, or a new venture, start with the problem, understand the trade-offs, and choose the path that fits.
enterprise-description: For companies evaluating Ethereum for products, operations, digital assets, or shared infrastructure.
institutions-description: For public agencies, public-interest organizations, and civil society exploring durable digital infrastructure.
founders-description: For teams building new Ethereum products and looking for programs, funding, and community support.
question-description: Ethereum can be useful when several parties need to share a record, settle value, verify a claim, or coordinate without agreeing on one party to own the infrastructure.
question-card-title: When a conventional system may be simpler
question-card-description: If one trusted organization can run the process alone, a conventional system may be the better fit. The right starting point is the coordination problem—not the technology.
purpose-description: These paths are educational starting points, not a vendor directory or an endorsement of a particular product, provider, or deployment. They explain the choices that determine whether a system remains open, secure, private, and workable for the people who rely on it.
